goshi_ambiguities.3 canonical form: Section 3 says the payload is strings, null and nested objects/arrays of the same, amounts as decimal strings, so JCS (RFC 8785) and codepoint-sorted compact JSON coincide. This module uses sorted-key compact JSON, which is JCS over that value domain extended to integers below 2^53 (JCS formats those as plain integers too; the intent scope carried in the manifest keeps the decision chain's integer amounts so that its digest is the digest of the same bytes); it refuses a float, a boolean or a non-BMP key rather than claim JCS for it.
goshi_ambiguities.3 action_hash: the text names action_hash without saying what is hashed. Farley's action_ref (F-2.2) hashes {agentId, actionType, scopeRequired, timestamp}, which is a different thing (a correlation anchor). Here action_hash is the SHA-256 of the executed action's argument bytes as the tool door hashed them, the same bytes the other three links hash; a verifier cannot check this without the manifest saying so (manifest.executed_action).
goshi_ambiguities.3 evidence_set_hash: not defined in the text. Here: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the sorted list of every evidence digest the packet cites (agent anchors, settlement anchor_hash, ledger entry). Re-derivable from the manifest; the construction is this module's.
goshi_ambiguities.3 ledger_entry_hash: the text speaks of a ledger slice, ledger events and ledger event hashes (4.1, 4.4, 5) without a format. Here a ledger event is {seq, type, at, data, prev_hash, event_hash}, event_hash = SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the event without event_hash, prev_hash the previous event_hash (genesis: 64 zeros); ledger_entry_hash is the event_hash of the event that recorded the decision the receipt states.
goshi_ambiguities.3 mandate_hash: named as the AP2 mandate_hash (4.2). A chain whose mandate is a person's signed approval, not an AP2 mandate, has no source for it: set to null, as 4.2 does for the network token id and the 3DS result when the implementation has no source. Whether null is allowed for mandate_hash is not said.
goshi_ambiguities.3 rail_anchors_hash: a receipt member; the settlement block of 4.3 has its own anchor_hash. The text does not say they are equal. Here rail_anchors_hash = the settlement anchor_hash, which is what lets Section 5's 'headline consistency across manifest, receipt' be checked at all.
goshi_ambiguities.3 key_id and signer_pubkey_hash: key_id is taken as equal to the envelope's kid and the payload's issuer_id (F-2.2: issuer_id MUST match kid); signer_pubkey_hash as SHA-256 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, hex. Neither construction is in the text.
goshi_ambiguities.3 timestamp and issued_at: the profile lists timestamp and the base draft requires issued_at; both are carried, timestamp read as the time of the decision stated, issued_at as the time the receipt was signed.
goshi_ambiguities.4.1 categories: the CE 3.0 / FPT view is a mapping of what the packet holds into three named categories with gap notes; the text defines no field names. Here: {category: {populated, value_or_null, gap_note}}. The verifier only checks that a category marked populated has a value, that the dispute reason code is present (4.1: a missing one MUST cause the mapper to raise), and that no category is populated from a source the manifest does not hold.
goshi_ambiguities.4.2 approval event hash: the text names an 'approval event hash' with no construction and no type. Here it is a typed digest {type, alg, digest} so a verifier can know which bytes to look for; the type is this repository's namespace. 4.2 says what the headline values are; it does not say which field of the executed action a BREACH names when several differ (here: the first differing key in sorted order), nor what intent scope and executed action look like (here: JSON objects carried in the manifest, each bound by digest to an item the packet also cites).
goshi_ambiguities.4.2 receipt_signature in agent_anchors: the block lists 'receipt signature' among agent-native facts: read as the hex signature of the dispute receipt itself, which the block then repeats. A block that carries it must carry the same value as the envelope.
goshi_ambiguities.4.3 anchor_hash: 'a canonical hash of the anchor content': here SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the block without anchor_hash (unanchored_fields included, since they are a statement about the content).
goshi_ambiguities.4.3 settlement versus headline: Section 5 asks for headline consistency; which headline the settlement amount is compared with is not said. Here: manifest.headline.amount_minor, which the manifest states as the amount in dispute; a mismatch is named SETTLEMENT_HEADLINE_MISMATCH (this module's name).
goshi_ambiguities.4.4 wrapper: acquisition record, custody record and authentication statement are described, not specified. Here: acquisition {captured_by, captured_at, tool, clock_source, gaps[]} (gaps declared, custodian never invented: captured_by MUST be present; 7: a host clock MUST be declared untrusted absent an external anchor), custody [{event, at, actor, ledger_event_hash}], authentication_statement {re_derivable: [names of checks]}.
goshi_ambiguities.5 failure names: the text names failures by example. SCOPE_HEADLINE_MISMATCH, SETTLEMENT_ANCHOR_HASH_MISMATCH and SETTLEMENT_UNANCHORED are the text's; every other code this verifier emits is its own.
goshi_ambiguities.F-2.1 envelope: the envelope shape only (payload + signature{alg, kid, sig}); the flat shape of F-2.1 and F-6.6 is refused, not verified, since the profile's receipt is a 'canonical dict' under an envelope.
